_metadata.independence: I read only u15-blind-input.json and no other file, repository content, web page or API before scoring.

hints.reason: Diamond is the proverbial hardest substance; a robot is only loosely hard (rigid metal body, hard-wired), so the robot side leans on a weak material property.

best_available.why: Only hint offered; the diamond side is unmistakable and a player can reach a metal robot through 'hard' with some effort.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The robot side of HARD is a shared-property stretch rather than a recognised scene; a hint like CUT or STEEL-style compound would serve better.

hints.reason: Diamond mine is a stock compound and rock is what is dug out of (and surrounds) a mine.
Diamond is the archetypal gem (near-hypernym), and rock reaches it through 'rocks and gems' collections and 'rock' as slang for a diamond ring.

best_available.why: Both sides are concrete and broad; no definitional lean.

pairs.pair_note: MINE is the clean serve. GEM passes but is close to naming the category diamond belongs to; the rock side is category-adjacent rather than a scene.

hints.reason: The 'diamond ring' effect of a total solar eclipse is real but specialist knowledge, while an eclipse is literally the moon's shadow.
Diamond-paned lattice windows are a niche architectural detail and a window casting a shadow is incidental; neither side is a route a player would recognise.

best_available.why: Shadow side is solid and the diamond-ring effect is at least a genuine, nameable fact for astronomy-aware players.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. ECLIPSE is the only defensible hint and it depends on niche eclipse lore; WINDOW is an invented route.

hints.reason: Diamonds are a playing-card suit and 'card shark' is a familiar phrase.

best_available.why: Two broad, independent, familiar routes meet cleanly.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent single hint.

hints.reason: Dew beading on a spider web is a recognisable scene and dewdrops are poetically called diamonds, but each side only works once the player already pictures the web.

best_available.why: Only hint; the dew-jewelled web is a genuine shared image even if neither word is reached directly.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The shared scene is real but poetic; many players will not get from DEW to DIAMOND without the web already in mind.

hints.reason: Diamond ring is the wedding jewel; 'spring wedding' is a familiar seasonal phrase though June and summer compete.
A baseball field is the diamond and spring training opens the baseball year.
Diamond is April's birthstone and April is a spring month; the birthstone fact is widely known but not universal.

best_available.why: Both routes are familiar compounds (baseball diamond, spring training).

pairs.pair_note: Three usable hints; BASEBALL strongest, APRIL needs birthstone knowledge, WEDDING is solid on diamond and fair on spring.

hints.reason: Diamonds sparkle and stars sparkle; a clean shared property.
'Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star ... like a diamond in the sky' ties both words together in one universally known rhyme.

best_available.why: The nursery rhyme names both targets, so it is a shared text and not just a shared property.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass; they are near-synonyms, so serving both gives little extra information.

hints.reason: Diamond heist and train heist (the Great Train Robbery) are both stock crime-story setups.

best_available.why: Two familiar crime-fiction compounds.

pairs.pair_note: Strong single hint.

hints.reason: Sparkling diamond is a stock description and sparkling water is a stock product.
Clarity is a defining diamond quality (the 'C' of clarity) and clear water is an everyday phrase.

best_available.why: Compound on the water side plus the diamond's signature property.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass comfortably.

hints.reason: The Wicked Witch covets the slippers in The Wizard of Oz, but they are ruby (silver in the book), never diamond, so the diamond side rests on a wrong fact.

best_available.why: Only hint offered; it reaches WITCH but has no honest path to DIAMOND.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Replace: the slippers route misremembers the gem.

hints.reason: Wolf fang is immediate; there is no recognised diamond route (diamond-studded grillz is not a familiar 'fang' scene).

best_available.why: Only hint offered; it is wolf-only filler.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Needs a fresh hint; FANG is wholly one-sided.

hints.reason: Both creatures have tails (dogs wag, dragons lash), but the property belongs to nearly every animal and singles out neither.
Toothless is the dragon in How to Train Your Dragon, famously written to behave like a big puppy; the dog side depends on knowing that characterisation (or an old toothless dog).

best_available.why: Dragon side is a named character; the puppy-like behaviour is a genuine shared trait for anyone who knows the films.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. TOOTHLESS is close to passing for the film's audience; TAIL is a shared property that does not distinguish.

hints.reason: Hunting dog and Easter egg hunt are both familiar compounds.
Eggs are the breakfast food; the dog side relies on the British idiom 'dog's breakfast' (a mess), which most non-UK players will not reach.

best_available.why: Two broad compounds.

pairs.pair_note: HUNT carries the pair; BREAKFAST is regional.

hints.reason: Fire hydrant is the compound and the dog-at-the-hydrant is a universal cartoon scene.
Dalmatian is a dog breed and the traditional firehouse dog.

best_available.why: Compound on the fire side plus an iconic dog scene.

pairs.pair_note: Two strong hints.

hints.reason: Zero is Jack Skellington's ghost dog in The Nightmare Before Christmas, a single character who is both targets.
Scooby-Doo is a cartoon dog whose entire franchise is chasing ghosts.

best_available.why: Universally known dog whose defining activity is ghosts.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass; ZERO is the more niche but still a fair single-character route.

hints.reason: Windows are glass; 'How Much Is That Doggie in the Window' and the dog-at-the-window scene cover the dog side.
Dog bowl is a compound and a glass bowl is an everyday object.

best_available.why: Compound on the dog side and material on the glass side; nothing to explain.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass.

hints.reason: Gold medal is immediate; dogs win medals only in dog shows or as decorated hero dogs, a thin route.
Retriever is a dog and 'golden retriever' delivers gold through its ordinary inflection.
Golden retriever reaches dog, but GOLDEN literally contains the target GOLD, which is a rule failure rather than a weak route.

best_available.why: Same golden-retriever route as GOLDEN without containing the target.

pairs.pair_note: RETRIEVER is the clean serve; GOLDEN fails only on contains_target; MEDAL is gold-heavy.

hints.reason: The heart is the symbol of love; dogs reach it through puppy love and the unconditional-love cliche of man's best friend.
Loyalty is the dog's defining virtue, but a 'loyal heart' is only a loose figurative phrase for the heart side.

best_available.why: Heart side is iconic and the dog side is a widely felt association.

pairs.pair_note: LOVE is a defensible shared-mood route like SWEET for APPLE+HONEY; LOYAL tilts to dog.

hints.reason: Sweetie and honey are interchangeable endearments (and honey is sweet); the dog side is only that people call their dogs sweetie, which applies to any pet or person.

best_available.why: Only hint offered; honey side is solid, dog side is a fond-owner stretch.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. SWEETIE behaves like a synonym of HONEY with a decorative dog side.

hints.reason: A pony is a small horse (near-synonym); the dog side is only the 'that dog is the size of a pony' joke about big breeds.
Horse race and dog (greyhound) race are both familiar betting sports.
Horses are the ranch animal and the ranch dog / cattle dog is a recognisable part of the same scene.

best_available.why: Both sides are established sports with the same word.

pairs.pair_note: RACE is clean; RANCH is a fair shared scene; PONY nearly names the horse.

hints.reason: Husky is a dog breed defined by hauling sleds across ice and snow.
Dog sled is a compound and sleds run on ice and snow.

best_available.why: Compound on the dog side and the sled's surface on the ice side.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass; HUSKY needs the breed's arctic image, which is widely held.

hints.reason: A chained dog is a stock image and chains are the stock iron object.

best_available.why: Concrete object on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: Strong single hint.

hints.reason: 'Sit' is the first dog command; no recognisable key route exists (a 'sit' key, dog-sitting with a house key, and sitting at piano keys are all invented).

best_available.why: Only hint offered; it is dog-only filler.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Needs a fresh hint.

hints.reason: King Charles is the monarch and the King Charles spaniel is a dog breed named for him.
Corgi is a dog; the royal association belongs to Queen Elizabeth, and the current King is known for not keeping corgis, so the king side is a generation off.

best_available.why: One name that is literally both a king and a dog breed.

pairs.pair_note: CHARLES is excellent; CORGI belongs with QUEEN rather than KING.

hints.reason: Hound is a synonym for dog; the knight side (medieval hunting hounds, 'The Hound' Sandor Clegane who is pointedly not a knight) is indirect.
Loyalty is the defining virtue of both the dog and the chivalric knight sworn to a lord.

best_available.why: A shared-property route like RICH for BANK+KING, with both sides strongly associated.

pairs.pair_note: LOYAL passes on shared virtue; HOUND nearly names the dog.

hints.reason: A laser is a beam of light and pets chasing a laser pointer is a recognisable scene, though cats own it more than dogs.
Guide dog and guiding light are both familiar compounds.

best_available.why: Compound on each side.

pairs.pair_note: GUIDE is strong; LASER passes with a cat-leaning dog side.

hints.reason: The mane is the lion's signature; only a few dog breeds (chow, Tibetan mastiff, the lion-cut Pomeranian) are described as maned.
A pride is a group of lions; there is no recognised dog route to 'pride'.

best_available.why: Lion side is iconic and maned dog breeds give a thin but real dog route.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. Both hints are lion-heavy; PRIDE is pure one-sided filler.

hints.reason: Laika was the Soviet space dog, but she orbited Earth on Sputnik 2 and never went to the moon, so the implied dog-on-the-moon route is a wrong fact and space-adjacent at best.
Dogs howl and howling at the moon is the stock image.

best_available.why: One scene that names both words.

pairs.pair_note: HOWL carries the pair; LAIKA is a space fact mis-aimed at the moon.

hints.reason: Cat and dog, cat and mouse: the cat is the shared partner of both.
Pluto is Mickey Mouse's pet dog.

best_available.why: Two universal pairings through one word.

pairs.pair_note: Both strong; PLUTO is a tidy single-character route.

hints.reason: Dogs howl and the howl-in-the-night scene is familiar, though the moon owns 'howl' more than night does.
Watchdog and night watch are both stock compounds.

best_available.why: Compound on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass; WATCH is the cleaner route.

hints.reason: Seals live in the ocean and are widely called sea dogs / ocean puppies for their dog-like faces and behaviour.
Doggy paddle is the swimming stroke and paddling in the ocean (or paddleboarding) is everyday.

best_available.why: Compound on the dog side and literal on the ocean side.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass; SEAL's dog side is a recognised likeness rather than a phrase.

hints.reason: Pirates sail the sea and 'sea dog' is the stock term for an old sailor or pirate.
Scurvy is the pirate's disease and 'ye scurvy dog' is the stock pirate insult.

best_available.why: Broad on both sides with the sea-dog compound.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass; SCURVY is a fun phrase route.

hints.reason: Corgi is a dog breed and the Queen's corgis are world-famous.

best_available.why: Breed plus iconic royal owner.

pairs.pair_note: Strong single hint.

hints.reason: Dog collar is immediate; the ring side is only that a collar is ring-shaped (or has a ring for the lead), a shape stretch.
Dog show is a compound and the show ring is where it happens.

best_available.why: One scene that holds both words.

pairs.pair_note: SHOW carries the pair; COLLAR is dog-heavy.

hints.reason: Spot is the classic dog name and the name of Boston Dynamics' widely seen robot dog.
K9 is the canine initialism and K-9 is Doctor Who's robot dog.
Aibo is Sony's robot dog; a single product that is both targets, but a brand many players will not know.

best_available.why: Familiar dog name plus the most-seen robot dog.

pairs.pair_note: All three are robot-dog references; SPOT is the broadest, AIBO the most niche.

hints.reason: Fetch is the dog's game; rocks are an incidental thing thrown, with sticks and balls far more typical.
Dogs are the archetypal pet and the pet rock is a famous novelty.

best_available.why: Compound on the rock side and category on the dog side.

pairs.pair_note: PET carries the pair; FETCH is dog-heavy.

hints.reason: Rosebud is a compound; the dog side comes from Bud/Buddy as a stock dog name (Air Bud).
Rose thorn is immediate; there is no recognised dog route (the thorn-in-the-paw fable is a lion, 'dog rose' is a botanical name few know).

best_available.why: Compound on the rose side and a familiar dog name.

pairs.pair_note: BUD passes on a name route; THORN is rose-only filler.

hints.reason: Dogs lick everything and a salt lick is a compound.
Sea salt and sea dog are both stock compounds.

best_available.why: Verb on the dog side, compound on the salt side, both broad.

pairs.pair_note: Two strong hints.

hints.reason: Homeward Bound is the lost-pets film whose golden retriever is named Shadow, so one title names both.
Dogs follow at your heels and a shadow follows you everywhere; 'follow like a shadow' is a stock phrase.

best_available.why: Shared verb that is defining for both words.

pairs.pair_note: Both pass; HOMEWARD rewards film knowledge.

hints.reason: Shark fin is iconic; dogs have no fins and the dogfish (a small shark) is too indirect to count.
Dog bite and shark bite are both stock phrases.

best_available.why: Same compound on both sides.

pairs.pair_note: BITE carries the pair; FIN is shark-only filler.
